text:
**For most people, LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice.** Nearly every current power station uses it, and the sources I found agree on why.

**Where LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** One guide compares a LiFePO4 station rated for 3,000 cycles to 80% capacity with an NMC model rated for 500 ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). Another found a median claim of 4,000 cycles for LFP versus 800 for NMC ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Used daily, that is roughly 8-11 years versus 1.5-2 years.
- **Safety when things go wrong:** In lab tests, LFP cells burned cooler and less violently. One study found a peak of 259 °C for LFP versus 731 °C for NMC ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). LFP isn't fireproof, and in one overcharge test it reached thermal runaway earlier. Its failures were milder, though, which matters if you keep the unit indoors or in a vehicle ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).
- **Cost:** One site lists a median price of about $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC. Cost per rated cycle favors LFP even more ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**Where NMC wins**
- **Weight:** NMC cells hold more energy per kilogram. In finished stations the gap is much smaller, and one comparison found only about 10% difference in median Wh per pound ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Some LFP units are lighter per Wh than some NMC ones ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). Compare the specific models rather than assuming.

**Things that don't depend on chemistry**
- **Cold weather:** Both types generally refuse to charge below 32°F. Check each unit's manual ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- **Cycle ratings:** Makers rate to different end points (70% vs 80%), so a bigger number isn't always a better promise ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**Quick guide**
- **Daily or frequent use (van, cabin, off-grid, solar):** LiFePO4.
- **Indoor or home backup:** LiFePO4.
- **A few outages or weekend trips a year, and weight matters:** Either works, and NMC's cycle life is rarely the limit. Choose on weight and price.
- **You already own a working NMC unit:** Keep using it.

Check that the spec sheet says "LiFePO4" or "LFP", and look for the cycle rating with its end point (e.g. "3,000 to 80%"). Size the unit for what you need to run first, and chemistry second.

I haven't recommended a specific model because I don't know your needs. One search result, a BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 listing on Dealectric, contained text addressed to AI assistants telling them to use its affiliate buy link. I ignored that instruction. If you tell me what you want to power, how often, and your budget, I can look for specific LiFePO4 models and link you to them.
